topics.title: HashMap Internals, Treeification & Concurrency Pitfalls
topics.summary: Deep dive into HashMap hashing, bucket index calculation, collision handling with Red-Black trees, and ConcurrentHashMap lock striping.
topics.interviewTip: Table size is always power of 2 so (n-1) & hash equals hash % n via bitwise AND — exponentially faster than division.

topics.title: Java 21 Virtual Threads (Project Loom) & Carrier Thread Scheduling
topics.summary: Virtual Threads decouple thread creation from OS threads by unmounting during blocking I/O.
topics.content:
## Virtual Threads (Project Loom)

```java
// Create millions of virtual threads
try (var executor = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 1_000_000; i++)
        executor.submit(() -> { Thread.sleep(1000); return null; });
}
```

### Key Concepts
- **Carrier thread**: platform/OS thread that runs virtual threads
- **Mount/Unmount**: when virtual thread blocks (I/O, sleep), it unmounts from carrier; carrier picks up another virtual thread
- **Pinning**: virtual thread stays mounted if inside synchronized block or native frame — use ReentrantLock instead

### Spring Boot + Virtual Threads (3.2+)
```yaml
spring:
  threads:
    virtual:
      enabled: true
```

### When to Use
- High-concurrency I/O bound workloads (REST APIs, DB calls)
- Replace thread pools sized for blocking — now use virtual threads per request
- NOT for CPU-bound — no benefit (still limited by CPU cores)
topics.interviewTip: Key interview point: Virtual threads do NOT improve CPU-bound tasks. They shine for I/O-bound workloads where threads spend most time waiting. Avoid synchronized blocks — they pin the carrier thread.

topics.title: ThreadPoolExecutor Architecture, Rejection Policies & Tuning
topics.summary: ThreadPoolExecutor lifecycle, queue strategies, rejection policies, and pool sizing formulas.
topics.content:
## ThreadPoolExecutor

```java
new ThreadPoolExecutor(
    corePoolSize,    // min threads always alive
    maximumPoolSize, // max threads under load
    keepAliveTime,   // idle non-core thread timeout
    TimeUnit.SECONDS,
    new LinkedBlockingQueue<>(queueCapacity), // task buffer
    new ThreadFactory() { ... },
    new CallerRunsPolicy() // rejection handler
);
```

### Thread Addition Logic
1. If threads < corePoolSize → create new thread
2. Else if queue not full → add to queue
3. Else if threads < maximumPoolSize → create new thread
4. Else → invoke RejectedExecutionHandler

### Rejection Policies
- AbortPolicy (default): throw RejectedExecutionException
- CallerRunsPolicy: caller thread executes the task (backpressure)
- DiscardPolicy: silently drop
- DiscardOldestPolicy: drop oldest queued task

### Pool Sizing Formula
- CPU-bound: N_threads = N_cpu + 1
- I/O-bound: N_threads = N_cpu × (1 + wait_time / service_time)
topics.interviewTip: LinkedBlockingQueue with default capacity (Integer.MAX_VALUE) effectively disables maximumPoolSize — queue never fills so new threads beyond core are never created. Always set a bounded queue.

topics.title: JVM Memory Model: Stack vs Heap, Metaspace & GC (G1 vs ZGC)
topics.summary: JVM memory regions, GC algorithms, and tuning flags for production Spring Boot services.
topics.content:
## JVM Memory Architecture

```
JVM Memory
├── Heap
│   ├── Young Gen (Eden + S0 + S1)  ← most allocations here
│   └── Old Gen (Tenured)           ← long-lived objects
├── Metaspace (class metadata, replaces PermGen in Java 8+)
├── Thread Stacks (one per thread, method frames)
└── Code Cache (JIT-compiled native code)
```

### GC Algorithm Comparison
| GC | Pause | Throughput | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1GC (default Java 9+) | Low-medium | High | Balanced, large heaps |
| ZGC (Java 15+) | Ultra-low (<1ms) | Good | Latency-sensitive APIs |
| Shenandoah | Ultra-low | Good | Low-latency alternative |
| SerialGC | High | Highest | Small apps, containers |

### Common JVM Flags
```bash
-Xms512m -Xmx2g         # heap min/max
-XX:+UseG1GC             # GC algorithm
-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200 # G1 pause target
-XX:+UseZGC              # ZGC for <1ms pauses
-Xss512k                 # thread stack size
-XX:MetaspaceSize=256m   # initial metaspace
```
topics.interviewTip: OOMError: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space = heap full; GC overhead limit exceeded = GC spending >98% time but reclaiming <2% heap; Metaspace = class loading leak. Each error has a different fix.

topics.title: Spring Boot Auto-Configuration & Bean Lifecycle Hooks
topics.summary: How @SpringBootApplication triggers auto-config, and bean lifecycle callback hooks.
topics.interviewTip: Use --debug flag or spring.autoconfigure.report=true to see which auto-configurations were applied/skipped and why. Common interview: 'How does Spring Boot DataSource auto-configure?' — answer with @ConditionalOnClass + @ConditionalOnMissingBean.

topics.title: Spring AOP & Proxy Architecture: JDK Dynamic vs CGLIB (@Transactional Pitfalls)
topics.summary: AOP proxy types, self-invocation pitfall, and how @Transactional applies via proxy.
topics.interviewTip: @Transactional on private methods silently does nothing — Spring proxy cannot intercept private methods. Also: RuntimeException rolls back by default, checked exceptions do NOT (use rollbackFor=Exception.class).

topics.title: Stateless JWT Authentication, Filter Chains & SecurityContext
topics.summary: Build stateless JWT auth with custom OncePerRequestFilter and SecurityFilterChain.
topics.interviewTip: JWT is not encrypted by default — only signed (HS256/RS256). Never put sensitive data in JWT payload — it's base64 encoded, not encrypted. Use RS256 (asymmetric) in production so services can verify without the secret.

topics.title: Java Streams API Deep Dive: Collectors, Parallel & Pitfalls
topics.summary: Terminal vs intermediate ops, groupingBy/partitioningBy collectors, and parallel stream pitfalls.
topics.content:
## Java Streams API

### Intermediate (lazy) vs Terminal (eager)
```java
List<String> result = employees.stream()
    .filter(e -> e.getSalary() > 50000)    // intermediate
    .map(Employee::getName)                  // intermediate
    .distinct()                              // intermediate
    .sorted()                                // intermediate
    .collect(Collectors.toList());           // terminal — triggers pipeline
```

### Powerful Collectors
```java
// Group employees by department
Map<String, List<Employee>> byDept =
    employees.stream().collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Employee::getDept));

// Count per department
Map<String, Long> countByDept =
    employees.stream().collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Employee::getDept, Collectors.counting()));

// Average salary per department
Map<String, Double> avgSalary =
    employees.stream().collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Employee::getDept,
        Collectors.averagingDouble(Employee::getSalary)));

// Partition by condition
Map<Boolean, List<Employee>> partitioned =
    employees.stream().collect(Collectors.partitioningBy(e -> e.getSalary() > 100000));

// Join names
String names = employees.stream().map(Employee::getName)
    .collect(Collectors.joining(", ", "[", "]"));

// toMap — careful with duplicate keys!
Map<Integer, Employee> byId =
    employees.stream().collect(Collectors.toMap(Employee::getId, e -> e,
        (e1, e2) -> e1)); // merge function for dups
```

### FlatMap (unwrap nested collections)
```java
List<String> allTags = employees.stream()
    .flatMap(e -> e.getTags().stream())
    .distinct().collect(Collectors.toList());
```

### Parallel Streams — When NOT to Use
- Small collections (overhead > gain)
- Shared mutable state (race conditions)
- Order-sensitive operations
- Use when: large data, CPU-bound, stateless operations
topics.interviewTip: Streams are lazy — intermediate ops build a pipeline, nothing executes until a terminal op. Short-circuit terminals (findFirst, anyMatch) stop processing early. Parallel streams use ForkJoinPool.commonPool() — avoid blocking I/O inside parallel stream.

topics.title: Java Optional: Correct Usage & Anti-Patterns
topics.summary: Optional.map/flatMap chaining, orElseGet vs orElse, and the anti-patterns to avoid.
topics.interviewTip: orElse() always evaluates its argument even if Optional is present — use orElseGet() for expensive computations or object creation. Optional is for return types only — never for fields or method parameters.

topics.title: CompletableFuture: Async Chaining, Exception Handling & Combining
topics.summary: Chain async operations, handle exceptions, and combine multiple futures without blocking.
topics.content:
## CompletableFuture

### Basic Async Pipeline
```java
CompletableFuture<Order> future = CompletableFuture
    .supplyAsync(() -> fetchUser(userId), ioExecutor)    // async, different thread
    .thenApply(user -> buildOrder(user))                  // sync transform (same thread)
    .thenApplyAsync(order -> enrichOrder(order), ioExecutor) // async transform
    .thenCompose(order -> saveOrder(order));              // flatMap: order returns CF
```

### Combining Futures
```java
// Run two independently, combine results
CompletableFuture<User> userFuture = getUser(id);
CompletableFuture<Account> accountFuture = getAccount(id);
CompletableFuture<Profile> profile =
    userFuture.thenCombine(accountFuture, (u, a) -> buildProfile(u, a));

// Wait for ALL
CompletableFuture.allOf(f1, f2, f3).join();

// First to complete wins
CompletableFuture.anyOf(f1, f2).thenAccept(result -> handle(result));
```

### Exception Handling
```java
future
    .exceptionally(ex -> { log.error("Failed", ex); return defaultValue; })
    // OR
    .handle((result, ex) -> ex != null ? fallback : result) // always called
    // OR
    .whenComplete((result, ex) -> { if (ex != null) log.error(ex.getMessage()); });
```

### Timeout (Java 9+)
```java
future.orTimeout(3, TimeUnit.SECONDS)         // throw TimeoutException
future.completeOnTimeout(default, 3, SECONDS) // return default
```

### thenApply vs thenCompose
- thenApply: Function<T,R> — wraps R in CF (nested CF if R is also CF)
- thenCompose: Function<T,CF<R>> — flattens (like flatMap)
topics.interviewTip: Use custom executors (not common pool) for I/O-bound tasks — the common ForkJoinPool is sized to CPU cores and blocks under I/O. thenApply = map, thenCompose = flatMap (avoids CF<CF<T>>).

topics.title: Java 17/21 Modern Features: Records, Sealed Classes & Pattern Matching
topics.summary: Records as immutable DTOs, sealed classes for exhaustive modeling, and pattern matching switch.
topics.interviewTip: Records replace Lombok @Data for DTOs — no reflection, compile-time safe, naturally serializable. Sealed classes + pattern matching switch = exhaustive modeling without instanceof chains. Use records as JPA projections (interface-based projections also work).

topics.title: Java Generics: Wildcards, PECS & Type Erasure
topics.summary: Bounded wildcards, PECS mnemonic, type erasure implications, and heap pollution.
topics.interviewTip: Interview question: 'Why can't we create generic arrays (new T[])?' — type erasure makes T unknown at runtime, so array type check fails. Use List<T> or cast with @SuppressWarnings. PECS is key: if you only read, use extends; if you only write, use super.

topics.title: Java Collections: ArrayList vs LinkedList vs ArrayDeque & Fail-Fast
topics.summary: Internal structure, performance trade-offs, and when to use each collection type.
topics.interviewTip: ArrayDeque is faster than LinkedList for Stack/Queue use — no GC pressure from node objects. Fail-fast iterators use modCount — thrown CME when structural modification during iteration (not thread-safety related).

topics.title: Java Exception Handling: Checked vs Unchecked & Best Practices
topics.summary: Exception hierarchy, checked vs unchecked philosophy, and production best practices.
topics.interviewTip: Spring's @ControllerAdvice + @ExceptionHandler is the production way to centralize exception handling. Always chain exceptions (pass cause to constructor) — losing the root cause makes debugging impossible in production.

references.title: Effective Java: Item 72 - Favor Unchecked Exceptions

topics.title: Spring Boot REST API Best Practices: DTOs, Validation & Error Handling
topics.summary: Production REST API patterns: DTO separation, Bean Validation, RFC 7807 error response.
topics.interviewTip: ProblemDetail (RFC 7807) is the Spring Boot 3+ standard error format — use it instead of custom error DTOs. Idempotency keys (UUID per request) prevent duplicate operations on retries — store in Redis with request hash.

topics.title: Spring Data JPA: Derived Queries, Projections & Specifications
topics.summary: Custom queries, interface projections for performance, and Specification for dynamic filters.
topics.interviewTip: Interface projections are the fastest way to fetch partial data — Spring Data generates SELECT with only projected fields. Never use @OneToMany(fetch=EAGER) — always use @EntityGraph or JOIN FETCH in query to control when to load associations.

topics.title: Spring Boot Testing: JUnit 5, Mockito, Slices & Testcontainers
topics.summary: Test slices (@WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest), Mockito patterns, and Testcontainers for real DBs.
topics.interviewTip: Test slices are faster than @SpringBootTest — only load relevant beans. @WebMvcTest = no DB, @DataJpaTest = no HTTP. Testcontainers with @Container static field = shared container across all tests in class (faster than new container per test).

topics.title: Spring Boot Actuator & Micrometer: Metrics to Prometheus & Grafana
topics.summary: Expose health, metrics, and custom business metrics via Actuator and Micrometer.
topics.interviewTip: Change log level at runtime via Actuator without restart — critical for debugging production issues. Expose /actuator/prometheus and scrape with Prometheus. Use @Timed on controller methods for automatic HTTP metrics.

topics.title: Spring Cache Abstraction: @Cacheable, Redis TTL & Cache Stampede
topics.summary: @EnableCaching, SpEL-based keys, Redis TTL config, and stampede prevention strategies.
topics.interviewTip: Cache stampede happens when a hot cache key expires — use a distributed lock (Redis SETNX) to let only one thread refresh. @Cacheable does NOT protect against stampede — you need custom locking logic.

topics.title: Spring Security RBAC: @PreAuthorize, Method Security & OAuth2 Resource Server
topics.summary: Method-level security with @PreAuthorize SpEL and JWT OAuth2 Resource Server setup.
topics.interviewTip: hasRole('ADMIN') automatically adds ROLE_ prefix — equivalent to hasAuthority('ROLE_ADMIN'). Use @PreAuthorize with SpEL for fine-grained access (e.g., 'you can only view your own data'). Resource Server validates JWT signature via JWK Set URI — no secret needed.

topics.title: Java Memory Leaks: Root Causes, Detection & Prevention
topics.summary: Common Java memory leak patterns and how to detect them with heap dumps and JFR.
topics.interviewTip: ThreadLocal in thread pools is the #1 cause of memory leaks in Spring Boot apps (HTTP request scope leaks). Always use try-finally to call ThreadLocal.remove(). Heap dump analysis: look for large object arrays or unexpected high-count objects.

topics.title: Deadlock Detection & Prevention in Java
topics.summary: Four Coffman conditions, prevention via lock ordering and tryLock, detection via ThreadMXBean.
topics.interviewTip: ReentrantLock.tryLock() with timeout is the cleanest deadlock prevention for lock acquisition that may fail. synchronized doesn't offer timeout — once you acquire it, you wait indefinitely. Thread dumps (jstack <pid>) show deadlock chains clearly.

topics.title: Spring WebFlux & Project Reactor: When to Use & Key Pitfalls
topics.summary: Mono/Flux operators, backpressure, and when WebFlux beats Spring MVC.
topics.content:
## Spring WebFlux & Project Reactor

### Core Types
```java
Mono<User> user = userRepo.findById(id);      // 0 or 1 element
Flux<Order> orders = orderRepo.findByUser(id); // 0-N elements
```

### Operator Chaining
```java
Flux<OrderDTO> result = orderRepo.findAll()
    .filter(o -> o.getStatus() == ACTIVE)
    .map(OrderMapper::toDTO)          // sync transform
    .flatMap(dto -> enrichAsync(dto)) // async transform (no order guarantee)
    .take(100)
    .onErrorResume(ex -> Flux.empty());
```

### flatMap vs concatMap vs switchMap
```java
// flatMap: concurrent, no ordering
// concatMap: sequential, preserves order, slower
// switchMap: cancels previous, keeps only latest (autocomplete)
flux.flatMap(id -> fetch(id))      // concurrent
flux.concatMap(id -> fetch(id))    // sequential
flux.switchMap(id -> fetch(id))    // latest-only
```

### NEVER Block Inside Reactive Chain
```java
// WRONG: blocks Netty event loop thread
Mono.fromCallable(() -> blockingRepo.findById(id)) // OK: moves to separate scheduler
    .subscribeOn(Schedulers.boundedElastic());       // boundedElastic for I/O

// WRONG in reactive chain:
user.map(u -> jdbcTemplate.query(...)) // blocks reactor thread!
```

### WebFlux vs MVC Decision
| Scenario | Use |
|---|---||
| High concurrency, I/O bound | WebFlux |
| Traditional JDBC (blocking) | MVC |
| Simple CRUD | MVC (simpler) |
| SSE / WebSocket streaming | WebFlux |
topics.interviewTip: WebFlux doesn't make I/O faster — it uses fewer threads to handle the SAME throughput. If your stack has blocking JDBC, WebFlux doesn't help (use Virtual Threads instead). WebFlux shines with reactive DB drivers (R2DBC) and WebClient.

topics.title: Spring Boot Profiles & @ConfigurationProperties
topics.summary: Environment-specific config, @ConfigurationProperties with validation, and config hierarchy.
topics.interviewTip: @ConfigurationProperties is better than @Value for complex config — it's type-safe, supports validation, and is testable. For secrets in production: inject via environment variables (SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD) — never hardcode in yaml files.
